To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the current control of a PWM converter with LCL-filter is possible without any current sensors.

(i) the current controller with a measured current is the best solution, (ii) the current controller based on the measured DC-link voltage is a good solution for a PWM rectifier, but not for an inverter, and (iii) the control structure with measured line current is not suitable for a PWM rectifer.

the current control with a line current sensor is more robust against line inductances variations, while the control with a DC-link voltage sensor is more robust with respect to the LCL-filter resonance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following aspects: * Analysis and comparison of two different current control structures * Active damping of the resonance of the LCL-filter * Experimental investigations on a 10 kW test bench
the design and control of a PWM converter with an LCL filter.

the following aspects: * Control strategies and their analysis * Experimental investigations * Comparison between different control structures PWM rectifier with LC-filter and different current control structures: Experimental investigations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current control using the line current is the best choice.
the current controller with a feedforward term is more robust and more efficient than the current controller with an additional feedforward term.
the use of a line current sensor is advantageous.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of the line current for current control and active damping is the best option.
a control scheme with a current measurement in the grid side of the converter and a voltage measurement at the DC-link is the best choice for the control of the PWM rectifier.
the use of the measured line current for current control leads to better results than the use of the converter current.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the current controller based on the DC-link voltage and the line current can be implemented in a very simple way and that it provides a very robust performance in terms of active damping, line inductance variation, etc. The
the current control structure with the line current as the only measured quantity is superior to the control structure with the converter current measurement.
the current control with the measured DC-link voltage is the most robust and flexible way to operate a PWM rectifier.
